summary: Renewal check-in focused on capacity upgrades (add Dedicated GPU pool), adding EU region for data residency, and contract extension options. Customer weighing hosted vs dedicated cost/latency tradeoffs; security and KMS/SSO requirements discussed. Agreed next steps: revised pricing, benchmarks, and providing prompt set and SLO targets.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intro, I'm Maya Chen, AE on the account, with Carlos from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Priya (BeaconHealth CTO): Doing well, thanks. We got a lot to cover — renewal's coming up and we want to scope expansion.
[00:22] Maya: Exactly. High-level agenda — capacity needs, adding EU region for data residency, and contract terms / timing. Carlos will go over perf and ops considerations.
[00:34] Carlos (Redwood SE): Hi all, quick note — I'll call out where we usually see latency hotspots and batching tradeoffs. Also, apologies in advance if I mispronounce PV C, sometimes my audio chat messes with acronyms.
[00:45] Liam (Head of ML): Haha, V P C, got it. For context our current usage: ~150 QPS at peak, mostly short prompts but some long clinical summarization with up to 6k tokens.
[00:57] Arjun (SRE): And from infra we need EU region for GDPR compliance for some patient data, plus separate key management — we'll want KMS in our account or HSM options.
[01:10] Maya: Great, that maps to the three asks we saw in your renewal questionnaire. Carlos, can you sketch Dedicated vs Hosted here?
[01:20] Carlos: Sure — hosted is simplest: we keep you on the Redwood API with region routing, but capacity is shared so burstiness may be throttled. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools (e.g., 8x-A100 or 16x depending on throughput) with predictable throughput and option to pin model variants. Cost per-token is lower with Dedicated for sustained high QPS.
[01:35] Priya: Do we get isolation and audit logs on Dedicated? That's non-negotiable for the regulated work.
[01:42] Carlos: Yes, Dedicated includes tenant isolation, audit logs, and you can integrate your KMS. For our Private offering you get a customer-managed control plane and V P C peering if needed — though that's a bigger lift.
[01:55] Nora (Procurement): Timeline question — if we sign extension now, when can we spin up EU capacity? We have a target go-live in mid-March.
[02:06] Maya: Realistically, Dedicated in an existing region can be turned up in ~4 weeks after PO and capacity reservation. EU region add-on can be 6-8 weeks depending on quota. We can prioritize it in the onboarding plan.
[02:18] Liam: On performance — our current 99th percentile latency spikes past 1.2s on some summarization calls; we need <800ms for the user-facing feature. Can Redwood hit that with 6k contexts?
[02:29] Carlos: Two levers — model size/context and batching. For 6k tokens we often recommend a quantized 32k-friendly variant with optimized attention kernels; also prefix/KV cache for common prompts. In Dedicated you can configure smaller batch windows to favor latency. We'll share a doc that shows deltas — I've seen 15-35% improvement depending on batch tuning.
[02:45] Priya: That sounds good. How about fallbacks? If a region goes down, do we failover to US and what about data residency?
[02:55] Maya: We do smart routing and fallback, but for EU-specific residency you'd want to use Dedicated or Private so data stays in-region. We can enable cross-region fallback only for non-sensitive traffic.
[03:06] Arjun: KMS integration — can we bring our own key and have HSM-level controls? We need auditability for key usage.
[03:15] Carlos: Yes, BYOK via customer-managed KMS is supported on Dedicated and Private. Audit logs include key usage events; for HSM-level we have a partner integration — we'll share the security whitepaper.
[03:27] Nora: On pricing, we got the baseline renewal quote but not the expansion SKU for EU region. We need line-item pricing for Dedicated capacity and EU add-on to circulate to finance.
[03:38] Maya: I'll send a revised quote with the Dedicated 8x-A100 pool, projected token discount tiers, and an EU region surcharge. Expect that by Thursday.
[03:47] Liam: For the benchmarks Carlos mentioned — please include both 8k and 32k contexts and token costs so we can model TCO.
[03:55] Carlos: Will do. Also I'll include an example batch config that hits <800ms 99th for samples I've run.
[04:03] Priya: Another item — our legal wants to extend contract by 12 months but with a performance SLA for 99th latency and uptime. Can Redwood commit to measurable SLOs?
[04:14] Maya: We have SLA options on Dedicated: uptime backed SLA and optional latency SLOs with runbooks and escalation paths. We'll include SLA language in the quote draft.
[04:25] Arjun: Regarding cutover — if we move some routes to Dedicated first, what's the usual migration plan? Zero-downtime?
[04:33] Carlos: Typical approach: canary route a small percentage of traffic to Dedicated, run parallel for 48-72 hours, verify metrics and then shift. We also support traffic mirroring for dry-run comparisons. Cutover is usually low-risk.
[04:46] Liam: A quick question on quantization — we've had hallucination concerns when using 4-bit in other stacks. Does Redwood's quant profiles affect model quality?
[04:56] Carlos: We recommend specific quant profiles per model and workload; for instruction-following tasks we often use int8 or mixed precision to balance quality. We'll include evals on your prompt set to show quality delta. If you see regressions we can adjust quant or fallback to fp16 on critical routes.
[05:12] Priya: Ok that gives confidence. On security questionnaire items — we still need SOC 2 Type II report, SAML SSO integration details, and network diagrams.
[05:22] Maya: I'll attach the SOC 2 report and SAML docs to the quote email. Carlos will include the network and architecture diagrams for Dedicated + V P C peering.
[05:32] Nora: Procurement needs to know cancellation terms if we commit to Dedicated for 12 months and then scale down.
[05:40] Maya: We have reserved capacity contracts with commit terms; there's usually a buyout or downgrade window — I'll include the exact contract language and cancellation schedule in the quote.
[05:50] Arjun: Any compliance differences between Dedicated and Private? If we need air-gapped later, what's that lift look like?
[05:58] Carlos: Private is more involved — customer-managed control plane and potentially on-prem package; typically multi-month engagement with our professional services. Dedicated is hosted but isolated and meets many compliance needs quicker.
[06:12] Liam: For immediate next steps we'll need: revised pricing, benchmark doc, and we'll share prompts and token distribution. Once finance signs off we can approve PO.
[06:22] Maya: Sounds good. To be explicit on dates: we'll shoot for quote by 2027-01-20, Carlos' benchmark by 2027-01-22, and you to share prompts by 2027-01-21.
[06:33] Priya: Works for us. Anything else on open risk? Latency budget and data residency are biggest.
[06:40] Maya: Understood. Final recap — Dedicated recommendation for predictable latency and cost with EU region add-on. We'll propose a phased rollout with canary routing.
[06:50] Nora: Thank you. We'll review the quote and get procurement timeline.
[06:55] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email and set a tentative technical deep-dive next week if needed.
[07:02] Liam: One quick micro-note — can you include per-route token-level cost breakdowns so we can map features to SKU?
[07:08] Maya: Yes, cost breakout per route included in the quote.
[07:12] Carlos: Also, FYI — there was a small typo in our earlier doc where KV cache was written as KV cash, so ignore that line.
[07:20] Priya: Good to know. Thanks all.
[07:24] Maya: End notes — action items and I'll send materials. Bye.
file_notes: Transcript intentionally preserves occasional transcription errors (e.g., 'V P C', 'KV cash') and informal speaker turns to resemble Fireflies exports. Document created for renewal/expansion topic: capacity upgrades, EU region addition, contract extension.
